items.followUp: Define a molecule and distinguish between homoatomic and heteroatomic molecules, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: A molecule is defined by its independent existence and retention of a substance’s chemical properties.
rubric.description: Defines a molecule as the smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and retain its chemical properties.

rubric.why: Homoatomic molecules contain atoms of only one element.
rubric.description: Identifies a homoatomic molecule as one made of atoms of the same element.

rubric.why: Heteroatomic molecules contain atoms of more than one element.
rubric.description: Identifies a heteroatomic molecule as one made of atoms of different elements.

rubric.why: Examples demonstrate both types of molecule.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a homoatomic molecule and a valid example of a heteroatomic molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for examples of both types.

modelAnswer: A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and retain its chemical properties.
A homoatomic molecule contains atoms of the same element; examples include H2 and O2.
A heteroatomic molecule contains atoms of different elements; examples include H2O and CO2.

items.followUp: Define ionic compounds and describe four of their important properties.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds consist of oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction.
rubric.description: Describes the ions and the attraction holding an ionic compound together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the nature of an ionic compound.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds usually have an ordered crystalline structure.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds are crystalline solids.

rubric.why: Strong attractions between ions require considerable energy to overcome.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds generally have high melting and boiling points.

rubric.why: Ions can move in molten or aqueous compounds but are fixed in the solid lattice.
rubric.description: States the electrical conductivity property of ionic compounds in molten or aqueous form, or their lack of conductivity as solids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct conductivity property.

rubric.why: Many ionic compounds dissolve in water or other polar solvents.
rubric.description: States that many ionic compounds are soluble in water or polar solvents.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are made of positive and negative ions formed by transfer of electrons and held together by electrostatic attraction.
They are usually crystalline solids.
They generally have high melting and boiling points because the attractions between their ions are strong.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not in the solid state.
Many ionic compounds are soluble in water or other polar solvents.

items.followUp: Define vapour pressure and explain how temperature and the nature of a liquid affect it.

rubric.why: Vapour pressure is the pressure of vapour in equilibrium with its liquid.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by vapour in equilibrium with its liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: A higher temperature enables more liquid molecules to enter the vapour phase.
rubric.description: States that vapour pressure increases as temperature increases.

rubric.why: The strength of attraction between liquid particles affects how readily they escape into the vapour phase.
rubric.description: Explains how the nature of a liquid, in terms of intermolecular forces, affects its vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship.

rubric.why: A non-volatile dissolved substance reduces the tendency of solvent molecules to escape into the vapour phase.
rubric.description: States that a dissolved non-volatile solute or impurity lowers vapour pressure.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid in a closed container.
Vapour pressure increases with an increase in temperature.
It depends on the nature of the liquid: stronger intermolecular forces give a lower vapour pressure, while weaker forces give a higher vapour pressure.
A dissolved non-volatile solute or impurity lowers the vapour pressure of the liquid.

items.followUp: Write four characteristics of a suspension.

rubric.why: A solution has a uniform composition throughout.
rubric.description: States that a solution is a homogeneous mixture.

rubric.why: The relative amounts of solute and solvent in a solution can vary.
rubric.description: States that the components of a solution can be present in variable proportions.

rubric.why: Dissolved particles remain dispersed and do not settle on standing.
rubric.description: States that solution particles do not settle on standing.

rubric.why: Dissolved particles pass through ordinary filter paper.
rubric.description: States that the components cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.

modelAnswer: A solution is a homogeneous mixture with uniform composition throughout.
Its components may be present in variable proportions.
Its particles do not settle on standing, so the solution is stable.
Its components cannot be separated by ordinary filtration because the dissolved particles pass through filter paper.

items.followUp: State two limitations of Rutherford’s atomic model.

rubric.why: According to classical physics, revolving electrons should radiate energy and eventually collapse into the nucleus, contradicting atomic stability.
rubric.description: States that Rutherford’s model could not explain atomic stability because revolving electrons should lose energy and fall into the nucleus.

rubric.why: The model did not account for the discrete line spectra emitted by atoms.
rubric.description: States that Rutherford’s model could not explain the line spectra of atoms.

modelAnswer: Rutherford’s model could not explain the stability of the atom: revolving electrons should radiate energy, lose energy and spiral into the nucleus.
It could not explain the discrete line spectra of atoms.

items.followUp: State how Mendeleev arranged elements in his periodic table.

rubric.why: Mendeleev arranged elements mainly according to increasing atomic mass.
rubric.description: States that elements were arranged in increasing order of atomic masses or atomic weights.

rubric.why: Placing elements with similar properties together in groups produced periodic repetition of their properties.
rubric.description: States that elements with similar properties were placed in the same groups or vertical columns.

modelAnswer: Mendeleev arranged the elements in order of increasing atomic masses (atomic weights).
He placed elements with similar chemical properties in the same vertical columns, called groups, so that their properties showed periodic repetition.
